Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2.

The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.369 of 2023 under sections 363, 366(A), 376,
506 IPC and under section 3/4 POCSO Act and under section 3(2)(VA), 3(2)(v) ST/ST Act, P.S.
Kaiserganj, District Bahraich.
3. Initially a missing person report was lodged alleging that the applicant on the false pretext of marriage had enticed away the daughter of the informant on 31.08.2023.
It was also alleged that the daughter of the informant was taken to Lucknow and thereafter she was left at Ghaghra Ghat.
It was Sonu Alias Mohammad Rasul vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Civil ...

1 also stated that when the daughter of the informant returned home, the FIR was lodged.

4. From the perusal of the FIR, it is clear that the incident is of dated 31.08.2023 and the FIR was lodged on 06.10.2023.
5.

The counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the statement of the victim recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., wherein the victim stated that at 11.00 pm night, when she had gone for easing herself, the applicant with two other persons took her on a vehicle to Dhawaria and thereafter they left her there for half an hour and after that, the applicant along with his accomplice came and three of them went to Jarwal Road.
It was also stated that the applicant had told that he would marry her and thereafter they went to Lucknow.
It was also alleged that physical relations were formed.
It was also stated that on the sixth day, the applicant dropped her at Ghaghra Ghat.
It was also stated that despite promising to marry, the applicant asked the victim to go away and she narrated these entire facts to his sister after four days of the incident.

It was also stated that the applicant had promised to take the victim on 16 day of the month whereas he did not come and thereafter he promise to be back on 28th and on the said date also, he did not come.
It was also stated that the applicant had married somewhere else.

Almost similar statement was given under section 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

It is argued that the entire case is based upon the allegations of forming physical relations on the false pretext of marriage and there is no averment as to what steps were taken by the applicant when she stayed for a period of five days at Lucknow.
The fact with regard to information given to the sister of the victim did not result in lodging of the FIR and the FIR in question was lodged after the applicant married somewhere else.
6. Learned AGA as well as the counsel for the informant strongly opposes the bail application.

7. Considering the statements and the law as explained in the of case of Deepak Gulati vs Tate of Haryana; 2013 (7) SCC 675 coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in jail since 08.10.2023, a case for bail is made out.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati vs Tate of Haryana; 2013 (7) SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Sonu Alias Mohammad Rasul be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.25000/-
(Twenty Five Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
